ledger.claim: The trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all describe a single trip: each carries trip_id TRP-00108, the trace runs from the recorded 07:19:20 start to the recorded 07:53:20 end, and the fare_breakdown's trip_id matches. The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) — same trip, matching identifier and pickup timestamp across the three artifacts — is therefore met on this bundle.

The trace governs the distance, not the rounded convenience copy: EV-GPS-00108 records trace_distance_km 26.17 over a 206-fix trace at 100% coverage, while the optimal route stored at booking is 21.0 km (EV-TRIP-00108). Measured against the booked optimal that is an excess of 5.17 km, or 24.62% of optimal, which clears both POL-RD-01 establishment tests — greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes. EV-GPS-00108 carries 206 fixes at a 10-second interval equal to the expected interval, coverage_pct 100.0 and max_gap_sec 0.0, so none of POL-RD-07(a), (b) or (c) fires; the excess may be measured from the trace itself and no independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii) is required.

The driver's 'I drove exactly where the app told me' is a rider-instruction defence under POL-RD-04, and it cannot be run: all four chat messages (EV-CHAT-00108) carry waypoint_hint null and not one names a road, so the 200 m corroboration test is undecidable on this record, the clause is unavailable, and under POL-RD-14 an instruction the trace does not corroborate excludes no distance from the excess.

No traffic advisory covers this trip. EV-ADVIS-00108-01 is MISSING, carries weight_multiplier 0.0 and fired issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — I disclose that impairment in the same claim. Under POL-RD-13 an external-cause excuse cannot be tested against an advisory that does not exist and carries no weight under POL-RD-08, so nothing in the bundle reduces the excess measured on the trace.

POL-RD-05 re-baselines the route to the amended endpoints — Punggol MRT to Changi T3 — and the rider does not dispute the endpoints she moved. What the re-quote cannot carry is the driver's admitted conduct: the trace shows two loops of the T3 departure kerb driven after the amended dropoff was reached, distance that sits inside the 26.17 km but outside any 'optimal route between the amended endpoints'. POL-RD-05 excludes that circling only 'where the rider was not at the amended point', and the only support for that is the driver's own statement, which cites no evidence ID and carries no weight under POL-RD-08.

If the excess is taken against the booked optimal route, POL-RD-02 makes the remedy arithmetic and the fare_breakdown supplies every input on its face: charged_total 33.77 less a recomputed fare of 27.63 (3.80 base + 0.75 x 21.0 km + 0.28 x 26.0 min + 0.80 platform fee), a refund of 6.14 rounded up to a payable 6.15 — above the 0.50 de minimis and far below the 90% full-refund share (0.18 of charged), so on that computation the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of the contested charge.

POL-RD-05 governs this trip, and the rider's 21.0 km arithmetic is run against the wrong itinerary. Both endpoints were amended after booking: the rider moved the pin to Punggol MRT PHV pickup bay at 07:12:30 (trip_record.pickup_amended_at) and, mid-journey, changed the destination to Changi Terminal 3 at 07:41:52 (trip_record.dropoff_amended_at). POL-RD-05 expressly covers a rider moving the pin, a rider giving a different address in the chat_log and a terminal change from T1 to T3, and it directs that POL-RD-01 be re-applied against the optimal route between the AMENDED endpoints. That route is a stored field on the trip record — amended_optimal_distance_km 24.60 with amended_optimal_duration_min 31.0 — and the tribunal must read it rather than re-derive it. The 21.0 km figure is the optimum between Blk 118 Rivervale Drive and Terminal 1, an itinerary that was never driven.

On the governing amended baseline the excess falls below the POL-RD-01 gate and no deviation exists. The trace measures 26.17 km — and POL-RD-01 says that where trace_distance_km and the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km (26.2) disagree, the trace governs — against an amended optimal of 24.60 km. That is an excess of 1.57 km, 6.4% of the optimal distance. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km; the percentage limb fails by a wide margin (6.4% against 20%), and both tests must pass. POL-RD-01 then says in terms that if either establishment test fails, no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip, the only exception being a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4), which does not arise on this fare breakdown.

The platform's default deviation block reports excess_km 5.17 and excess_pct 24.62 only because it measures the driven trace against the superseded booked optimum of 21.0 km. POL-RD-05 forbids exactly that substitution and adds that distance driven before an amendment timestamp is never counted as excess against the driver. The booked optimum predates both amendment timestamps recorded on the trip record, and the extra distance the rider now objects to is the Punggol-to-Terminal-3 leg that she herself asked for. Once POL-RD-01 is re-run on the amended route, the threshold test fails and the rider's 'this trip is usually 21 km' comparison drops out of the case.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it. The trace she would have to rely on is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 206 fixes at a 10 second sample interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, and no POL-RD-07(a)-(c) defect — so the trace is admissible and clean, but what it shows on the amended baseline is an excess of 1.57 km, i.e. 6.4%, which does not meet the POL-RD-01 threshold limb (b) requires her to prove. Her profile does not rescue the claim either: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the 4-or-more that POL-RD-08's enhanced-corroboration test requires, so no additional corroboration is called for and none is offered.

The rider's complaint that the driver 'drove around the airport for another five minutes' does not carry the claim, even taken at its highest. POL-RD-05 excludes from excess the distance driven around an amended dropoff point where the rider was not at it and the trace shows the vehicle circling within 400 m; and the excess on the amended baseline is already only 1.57 km, below the POL-RD-01 gate, before any such exclusion is applied. Whatever happened on the Terminal 3 kerb approach, it cannot convert a 6.4% variance into a refundable deviation, because the threshold is a single numeric gate that ordinary manoeuvring does not open.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern to weigh against the driver. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 402, so neither limb of the POL-RD-06 test is met — not 3 or more flags, and not the 0.05 ratio (which would require 21 flags) with the 40-trip floor satisfied. POL-RD-06 is in any event not engaged on this trip, because no MATERIAL deviation (greater than 50% or greater than 8.0 km of excess) is recorded once the amended baseline is used. Only the two profile fields POL-RD-06 names have been cited here, as POL-GEN-01 requires.

The pass-through layer produces nothing for the rider either. The fare breakdown carries tolls_erp 0.00 with an empty erp_gantries list, waiting_time_fee 0.00, and airport_surcharge 0.00 — correctly so, because this trip ENDS at Changi rather than originating there, and no surcharge is chargeable or charged. There is therefore no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge for POL-RD-09(4) to correct as a standalone billing-integrity refund, and no off-route ERP to be itemised or added on top of anything. The charging lines on this trip all have counterparts in the trace and trip record.

No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-00108-01 is MISSING, carries weight_multiplier 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, which is disclosed here as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. That absence decides nothing in this case, because the driver has never asserted an external traffic cause that would need an advisory to be tested under POL-RD-03 or discarded under POL-RD-13. His explanation is the rider's own two endpoint amendments in the chat log — 'ok noted' at 07:12:15 and 'ok changing now' at 07:42:05 — and it is supported on the record by the stored amended-optimal figures, not by any assertion about conditions on the road.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you accept the same trip: TRP-00108, metered product RYDE_X, charged SGD 33.77 and paid (EV-FARE-00108, EV-TRIP-00108). The whole dispute is which 'optimal route' the distance should be measured against.

To the rider: your 21.0 km figure is the booked route from Blk 118 Rivervale Drive to Changi Terminal 1 — an itinerary that was never driven. The record shows you moved the pickup pin to Punggol MRT PHV bay at 07:12:30 (trip_record.pickup_amended_at) and, mid-journey, changed the destination to Changi Terminal 3 at 07:41:52 (trip_record.dropoff_amended_at); both are confirmed in the chat log (EV-CHAT-00108: 'im at punggol mrt phv pickup bay instead, moved the pin' at 07:11:58, and 'sorry ah can change to T3?' at 07:41:40, acknowledged 'ok changing now'). POL-RD-05 governs exactly this situation — a rider moving the pin, a rider giving a different address in the chat log, and a T1-to-T3 terminal change are all named in it — and it directs that POL-RD-01 be re-applied against the optimal route between the amended endpoints. That figure is stored on the trip record as amended_optimal_distance_km 24.60 km with amended_optimal_duration_min 31.0, and it is to be read, not re-derived.

On that amended baseline there is no deviation. The trace EV-GPS-00108 (weight 1.0; 206 fixes, 10 s interval, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0, no POL-RD-07 defects) measures trace_distance_km 26.17, and POL-RD-01 provides that the trace governs over the rounded 26.2 km convenience copy on the trip record. Excess = 26.17 − 24.60 = 1.57 km, which is 6.4% of 24.60 km. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only when the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km absolute; the percentage limb fails, so no deviation exists and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised.

This disposes of the rider's two money claims, which are rejected. The excess of 5.17 km / 24.62% is the platform's default deviation block measuring against the superseded 21.0 km booked route; POL-RD-01 requires materiality to be assessed on the excess remaining after a POL-RD-05 adjustment. The proposed POL-RD-02 refund of SGD 6.15 (charged_total 33.77 less recomputed_fare 27.63) is rejected because POL-RD-02 runs only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01, and none is.

The rider's point about the driver 'driving in circles' at Terminal 3 does not change the outcome. Even counting the T3 kerb manoeuvres inside the excess, the excess is only 1.57 km, far below the gate; and POL-RD-05 excludes such within-400 m circling from excess in the driver's favour, not the rider's. The driver's account that the rider was not at the kerb is a counterparty statement, which carries no weight_multiplier and cannot carry a citable fact; the result is the same without it.

To the driver: nothing further is owed to you either. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00108) bills 26.2 km against a 26.17 km trace, so there are no unbilled kilometres and no POL-RD-04 driver compensation. There are no toll or ERP lines (SGD 0.00, empty erp_gantries) and no airport surcharge (SGD 0.00), which is correct because this trip ENDS at Changi rather than originating there, so there is no phantom charge for POL-RD-09(4) to refund and no billing-integrity referral.

No repeat-deviation pattern arises under POL-RD-06: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across completed_trips_90d of 402, so neither limb of the test is met, and no material deviation is recorded in any event; no driver-conduct referral follows. No traffic advisory is on file — EV-ADVIS-00108-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — but neither party asserts an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 and POL-RD-13 are not engaged and nothing turns on its absence. No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires: the trip identifiers match across all three artifacts, the trace is unimpaired, no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing or field-deficient artifact, no timestamp disagreement exists, and the sides are not supported by comparable-strength contradictory evidence.

Confidence is 0.9. The deciding facts — the two recorded endpoint amendments and the amended re-quote, the governing trace distance, and the chat log confirming the amendments — are carried by EV-TRIP-00108, EV-GPS-00108 and EV-CHAT-00108, each at weight 1.0, so no discount applies and the ruling is well above the 0.70 floor.

Outcome: NO_ACTION. The filing party's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands — the SGD 33.77 charge and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 are left as they are; no money moves. This provisional ruling may be appealed once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
